item.text:
**Reused Evidence**
None from the earlier chapter threads adds materially new 5B evidence beyond the local priors and broad office context.

**New Evidence**
1. IMF says 2022 growth was solid, but the fiscal stance still loosened under Bolsonaro-era policy.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Brazil: 2023 Article IV Consultation-Press Release; Staff Report; Staff Supplement; and Statement by the Executive Director for Brazil","publisher":"International Monetary Fund","publication_date":"2023-07-31","url":"https://www.imf.org/en/publications/cr/issues/2023/07/31/brazil-2023-article-iv-consultation-press-release-staff-report-staff-supplement-and-537328","claim":"IMF staff said Brazil's real GDP growth was 2.9% in 2022, the nonfinancial public sector primary surplus rose to 1.3% of GDP, gross debt fell to 85.9% of GDP, and the fiscal stance nevertheless turned expansionary in 2022 because of broad tax cuts on essential goods and services and higher social support.","locator":"Summary and paragraph 9 of the staff report","source_type":"IGO","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Authoritative IMF country report with detailed macro and fiscal analysis for the target year.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Directly covers 2022 with retrospective analysis published in 2023.","ruler_attribution":"Mixed attribution: the macro outcome reflects Bolsonaro-era policy choices, commodity revenues, and independent monetary policy rather than Bolsonaro alone.","contrary_evidence":["The same report credits record commodity revenues and a wage/hiring freeze for much of the fiscal improvement, so not all positive movement is attributable to Bolsonaro."],"lenses":["5B.3","5B.9","5B.10"]}
2. IBGE shows 2022 inflation cooled from 2021, but it was still well above target.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"IPCA vai a 0,62% em dezembro e fecha 2022 em 5,79%","publisher":"IBGE","publication_date":"2023-01-10","url":"https://agenciadenoticias.ibge.gov.br/agencia-sala-de-imprensa/2013-agencia-de-noticias/releases/36047-ipca-vai-a-0-62-em-dezembro-e-fecha-2022-em-5-79","claim":"IBGE reported that Brazil's IPCA ended 2022 at 5.79%, down from 10.06% in 2021.","locator":"Opening summary and table of annual results","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Primary national statistics release for the consumer price index.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Directly measures the target year 2022.","ruler_attribution":"National outcome under Bolsonaro's last year in office, but heavily affected by external price shocks and monetary policy beyond his direct control.","contrary_evidence":["Inflation improved versus 2021, so 2022 was not a straight-line deterioration."],"lenses":["5B.3","5B.9"]}
3. The central bank said 2022 was a target miss and explained it publicly.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Our Results","publisher":"Banco Central do Brasil","publication_date":"2023","url":"https://www.bcb.gov.br/en/publications/our_results_2022","claim":"The BCB said the 2022 inflation target was 3.5% with a 1.5 percentage point tolerance band, but inflation reached 5.79%, and the causes were explained in an open letter.","locator":"Opening section on stability of purchasing power","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Primary central-bank annual report summarizing the year and the target miss.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Directly about 2022 results, published as the 2022 annual report.","ruler_attribution":"Attribution is limited because the BCB is institutionally autonomous; this is context for Bolsonaro-era macro management, not a direct presidential act.","contrary_evidence":["The report emphasizes BCB policy implementation, so the evidence is about the macro regime rather than Bolsonaro personally."],"lenses":["5B.3","5B.7","5B.9"]}
4. The labor market recovered in 2022, but unevenly and with high underutilization.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Continuous PNAD: in 2022, average annual unemployment rate was 9.3%, average annual underutilization rate was 20.8%","publisher":"IBGE","publication_date":"2023-02-28","url":"https://agenciadenoticias.ibge.gov.br/agencia-press-room/2185-news-agency/releases-en/36358-continuous-pnad-in-2022-average-annual-unemployment-rate-was-9-3-average-annual-underutilization-rate-was-20-8","claim":"IBGE reported an average annual unemployment rate of 9.3% in 2022, an average employed population of 98.0 million, and average labor underutilization of 20.8%.","locator":"Highlights section and summary table","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Primary national labor-market statistics release for 2022.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Directly measures the target year 2022.","ruler_attribution":"Mostly context and outcome: labor recovery occurred under Bolsonaro but was also shaped by the pandemic rebound and macro conditions.","contrary_evidence":["The level remained high by historical standards, so the recovery was partial rather than decisive."],"lenses":["5B.9","5B.10"]}
5. Household income and redistribution improved in 2022, with Auxílio Brasil part of the story.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"In 2022, labor market and \"Auxílio Brasil\" cash transfer program allow income recovery","publisher":"IBGE","publication_date":"2023-05-11","url":"https://agenciadenoticias.ibge.gov.br/en/agencia-news/2184-news-agency/news/36873-em-2022-mercado-de-trabalho-e-auxilio-brasil-permitem-recuperacao-dos-rendimentos-3","claim":"IBGE said average real monthly household income per capita reached R$1,586 in 2022, up 6.9% from 2021, the Auxílio Brasil/Bolsa Família beneficiary share in households rose to 16.9%, and the Gini index for household income per capita fell to 0.518, the lowest in the series.","locator":"Highlights section and inequality discussion","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Primary statistics release with explicit 2022 income and inequality estimates.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Directly about 2022.","ruler_attribution":"Mixed: the income recovery reflects labor-market rebound and social-transfer policy under Bolsonaro's administration, not Bolsonaro alone.","contrary_evidence":["The article itself notes that benefit-category shifts may partly reflect respondent confusion and migration between programs."],"lenses":["5B.8","5B.10","5B.6"]}
6. Households remained very unevenly positioned across regions in 2022.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"IBGE releases per capita household earnings 2022 for Brazil and Federation Units","publisher":"IBGE","publication_date":"2023-02-24","url":"https://agenciadenoticias.ibge.gov.br/en/agencia-press-room/2185-news-agency/releases-en/36327-ibge-releases-per-capita-household-earnings-2022-for-brazil-and-federation-units","claim":"IBGE reported Brazil's nominal monthly household income per capita at R$1,625 in 2022, ranging from R$814 in Maranhão to R$2,913 in the Federal District.","locator":"Summary table for Brazil and federation units","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Primary national statistics release with state-level 2022 values.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Directly measures 2022 household income distribution.","ruler_attribution":"Mostly inherited and structural, though it sets the baseline for assessing Bolsonaro-era distributional performance.","contrary_evidence":["The measure is descriptive rather than causal, so it cannot on its own prove presidential responsibility for regional gaps."],"lenses":["5B.8","5B.10"]}
7. Poverty stayed high in 2022 even as it improved later.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"In 2023, poverty in the country drops to lowest level since 2012","publisher":"IBGE","publication_date":"2024-12-04","url":"https://agenciadenoticias.ibge.gov.br/en/agencia-news/2184-news-agency/news/42113-in-2023-poverty-in-the-country-drops-to-lowest-level-since-2012","claim":"IBGE reported that poverty in Brazil stood at 31.6% in 2022 and extreme poverty at 5.9%, before both rates fell in 2023.","locator":"Highlights section and poverty summary paragraphs","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Primary statistical release that provides the 2022 baseline and 2023 comparison.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Retrospective but directly states the 2022 target-year baseline.","ruler_attribution":"Contextual baseline for Bolsonaro's last year; the later improvement does not itself prove 2022 policy causation.","contrary_evidence":["Because the article is retrospective, it is better for baseline and trajectory than for sharp attribution."],"lenses":["5B.8","5B.10"]}
8. Bolsonaro-era emergency policy used fiscal room for transfers and fuel relief.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Emenda Constitucional nº 123","publisher":"Presidência da República / Planalto","publication_date":"2022-07-14","url":"https://planalto.gov.br/ccivil_03/constituicao/emendas/emc/emc123.htm","claim":"The amendment recognized a 2022 state of emergency from fuel-price spikes and expanded Auxílio Brasil by R$200 per month from August to December 2022, while authorizing fuel-tax relief and transport aid.","locator":"Arts. 3 and 5","source_type":"legal","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Primary constitutional amendment with explicit benefit and tax-relief provisions.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Direct 2022 enactment and implementation window.","ruler_attribution":"Enacted during Bolsonaro's presidency and implemented by his administration, though the legislative coalition and Congress drove the measure.","contrary_evidence":["This is short-term relief policy; it does not prove durable productivity gains or fiscal sustainability."],"lenses":["5B.1","5B.6","5B.8","5B.9"]}
9. The government operationalized the higher Auxílio Brasil payment during 2022.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Ministério da Cidadania antecipa calendário do Auxílio Brasil em agosto","publisher":"Ministério da Cidadania","publication_date":"2022-07-25","url":"https://www.gov.br/pt-br/noticias/assistencia-social/2022/07/ministerio-da-cidadania-antecipa-calendario-do-auxilio-brasil-em-agosto/","claim":"The ministry advanced the August 2022 payment schedule and said the program's minimum benefit would be R$600 starting August 9 under PEC 1/22.","locator":"Opening paragraphs","source_type":"official","source_confidence":"high","source_confidence_reason":"Contemporaneous government implementation notice for the cash-transfer increase.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Directly in 2022.","ruler_attribution":"Directly attributable to Bolsonaro's administration as the implementing executive authority.","contrary_evidence":["The increase was temporary and tied to the election-year emergency package."],"lenses":["5B.6","5B.8","5B.9"]}
10. Bolsonaro staffed part of the economic apparatus with a fiscal-policy technocrat.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Governo exonera presidente do Ipea e nomeia auxiliar de Guedes como substituto","publisher":"UOL / Reuters","publication_date":"2022-03-09","url":"https://economia.uol.com.br/noticias/reuters/2022/03/09/governo-exonera-presidente-do-ipea-e-nomeia-auxiliar-de-guedes-como-substituto.htm","claim":"The government dismissed the IPEA president and named Erik Figueiredo, then the Economy Ministry's subsecretary of fiscal policy, as his replacement to make the institute more propositive.","locator":"Lead paragraphs and the description of Figueiredo's prior role","source_type":"media","source_confidence":"medium_high","source_confidence_reason":"Reuters reporting through a major Brazilian outlet on a concrete appointment inside the economic policy apparatus.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Directly in 2022.","ruler_attribution":"Direct Bolsonaro-administration appointment, but the evidence is about staffing rather than economic outcomes.","contrary_evidence":["A technocratic appointment is only weak evidence of competence unless paired with results."],"lenses":["5B.2","5B.7"]}
11. Bolsonaro openly favored loosening the spending cap for post-election infrastructure.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Brazil's Bolsonaro vows to change spending cap rule after election","publisher":"Euronews / Reuters","publication_date":"2022-04-30","url":"https://www.euronews.com/2022/04/30/us-brazil-economy-bolsonaro","claim":"Bolsonaro said he intended to change the spending cap after the October election to make room for higher infrastructure spending.","locator":"Lead paragraphs and direct quote in the article","source_type":"media","source_confidence":"medium_high","source_confidence_reason":"Reuters reporting with a direct Bolsonaro quote and clear policy context.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Directly in the 2022 election year.","ruler_attribution":"Direct Bolsonaro statement and preference.","contrary_evidence":["The proposal was deferred until after the election, which makes the motive look partly electoral rather than technocratic."],"lenses":["5B.3","5B.6","5B.7","5B.10"]}
12. Short-term fiscal results improved, but only with restraint and a tight spending cap.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Brazil government improves primary budget deficit forecast for 2022","publisher":"Reuters","publication_date":"2022-07-22","url":"https://www.investing.com/news/economy/brazil-government-improves-primary-budget-deficit-forecast-for-2022-2852255","claim":"Brazil's government lowered its 2022 primary deficit forecast because of booming tax collection, but also froze R$6.739 billion in spending to comply with the spending cap.","locator":"Lead paragraph and fiscal update","source_type":"media","source_confidence":"medium_high","source_confidence_reason":"Reuters reporting on official fiscal figures and the spending-freeze response.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Directly in 2022.","ruler_attribution":"Mixed: revenue windfalls were external, while the spending freeze was a policy response by Bolsonaro's government.","contrary_evidence":["The improved fiscal outlook was helped by record tax and royalty revenues, so it was not purely a policy success."],"lenses":["5B.3","5B.9","5B.10"]}
13. Bolsonaro's budget choices in January 2022 favored payroll and election spending over discretionary spending.
SOURCE_CLAIM_JSON: {"title":"Brazil government to veto 3.1 billion reais in budget items to fund payroll -sources","publisher":"Reuters","publication_date":"2022-01-21","url":"https://www.investing.com/news/economic-indicators/brazil-government-to-veto-31-billion-reais-in-budget-items-to-fund-payroll-sources-2745305","claim":"The government planned to veto R$3.1 billion in budget items to fund payroll, while leaving the electoral fund at R$4.9 billion, a politically difficult choice in an election year.","locator":"Lead paragraph and the section on the electoral fund and payroll allocations","source_type":"media","source_confidence":"medium_high","source_confidence_reason":"Reuters reporting based on Ministry of Economy sources and the official budget process.","final_evidence_use":"final_evidence","period_fit":"Directly in the 2022 budget cycle.","ruler_attribution":"Bolsonaro administration budget choice, but shaped by Congress and election-year politics.","contrary_evidence":["The decision was partly constrained by Congress already having approved the budget bill."],"lenses":["5B.1","5B.3","5B.5","5B.7"]}

**Search and Rejection Summary**
I reviewed roughly 30 documents across IBGE releases, Banco Central reports and Copom materials, IMF Article IV material, Planalto constitutional and legal texts, Ministry of Cidadania implementation notices, Reuters/UOL reporting, and a smaller number of broader Brazil-economy explainers.

Retained because they added distinct evidence:
- IMF and BCB materials for macro stability, inflation, and debt.
- IBGE labor, income, inequality, and poverty releases for household welfare and distribution.
- EC 123 and Auxílio Brasil notices for direct policy action on transfers and fuel relief.
- Reuters/UOL reporting for appointment choices, spending-cap intentions, and election-year fiscal priorities.

Rejected or de-prioritized:
- Duplicate Reuters mirrors of the same story once one version was kept.
- Generic 2022 Brazil economy explainers that repeated the same macro facts without new attribution.
- Broad commodity-price or global-inflation commentary that did not change the ruler-specific analysis.
- Post-2023 retrospectives that did not add a new 2022 fact beyond the IBGE/IMF releases already kept.
- Sources focused on political or electoral conflict rather than economic well-being.

**Remaining Gaps**
- Direct evidence on Bolsonaro's own competence as an economic manager is still mixed because many 2022 outcomes came from the labor-market rebound, commodity revenues, and the independent central bank rather than from presidential control alone.
- The strongest ruler-specific positives are the 2022 transfer package, the Auxílio Brasil expansion, and appointment/staffing choices. The strongest negatives are fiscal looseness, election-year spending priorities, and the willingness to loosen the spending cap.
- I still have only partial evidence on whether economic gains were distributed fairly across genders, racial groups, and regions once social transfers are separated from labor-market recovery.
- More search would help on 2022 tax expenditure beneficiaries, public-investment execution, and whether Bolsonaro empowered or sidelined technocrats in the finance and planning apparatus.
